machine: Ryzen AI MAX+ 395 / Radeon 8060S / XDNA2, 128 GB, Arch (Omarchy), Linux 7.2.15; power profile performance; machine quiet (load under 1, GPU idle before each run)
software: llama.cpp b10944 Linux Vulkan release (libggml-vulkan.so sha256 c25c5ac2...869e06), Mesa 26.2.5 RADV, xrt 2.21.75, zest: the quantized-weight kernel in the backend (the commit after 69f90d1), with GGML_XDNA_WEIGHTS=auto as it then was
method: zest llama-bench -ngl 99 -n 0 -b 2048 -ub 2048, one configuration at a time; tokens/s is the median of the timed repetitions (3 unless noted), after llama-bench's warm-up prompt

prefill_tokens_s.configuration: zest, GGML_XDNA_WEIGHTS=bfp16 (49 layers on the NPU)
zest, GGML_XDNA_WEIGHTS=auto (the default when measured; since removed)
prefill_tokens_s.note: the same pieces, multiplies and calls as bfp16: no weight goes to the quantized kernel (see findings)

prefill_tokens_s.configuration: zest, GGML_XDNA_WEIGHTS=quant (64 layers on the NPU)
zest, quant, quantized kernel rebuilt with the restructured multiply loop (GGML_XDNA_QKERNELS)
zest, bfp16, GGML_XDNA_MAX_COPY_GB=28 (64 layers on the NPU, 25.8 GB of copies)

chunk_of_2048_tokens_s.method: GGML_XDNA_TRACE=1 GGML_XDNA_TRACE_EVERY=1, per-piece lines summed per chunk; 'npu' is the time the host waited on the NPU (two streams overlap host work with it), 'outside' is the chunk less zest's pieces: the GPU's share and scheduling
chunk_of_2048_tokens_s.projection_flop: the 64 layers' weight multiplies are 99.7 TFLOP a chunk (48.66 GFLOP a token; the feed-forward ones are 70%); the GPU alone spends about 4.7 s on them (5.91 less the 1.2 s left when zest takes them all): about 21 TFLOPS

bfp16_kernel_m1024.method: build/bench-npu-gemm, median of 10-20, the 27B's seven projection shapes

quantized_kernel_m1536_ms.method: 24 multiplying cores, real Q4_K weights, 1536x17408x5120 and 1536x5120x17408, interleaved, best of 4 rounds of 5; x3 = the chunk's multiply repeated three times per chunk (timing build)
quantized_kernel_m1536_ms.restructured_vs_shipped: outputs bit-identical (0 words differ) in fp32 and bf16 output modes

rows_sweep_ms.note: linear in rows: no fixed cost per call

unpack_repeated.method: restructured loop, bf16 sums; the unpacking core unpacks each tile 1, 2 and 3 times (timing build)
unpack_repeated.reading: about 12.8 ms per unpack of the call's weights, and the GEMM takes one unpack plus under 1 ms: the unpacking core sets the pace (542 MB a call at 40.7 GB/s; the DRAM port carries about 57)

beside_the_gpu.method: bench-npu-gemm (BFP16 kernel, median of 150) looping while llama-bench -dev Vulkan0 pp2048 runs
beside_the_gpu.gpu_tokens_s: 329 with the NPU busy about two thirds of the time (344-345 once it stops)

correctness.method: llama-perplexity -c 512 -b 2048 -ub 2048 --chunks 8 over README.md + specs/xdna-backend/spec.md, against the GPU's logits; and 24 greedy tokens after a 500-character prompt (GGML_XDNA_MIN_BATCH=32)
correctness.quant_64_layers_restructured_loop: identical to quant to the last printed digit
correctness.bfp16_64_layers: identical to quant to the last printed digit: the quantized kernel gives the BFP16 kernel's answers on the whole model
correctness.greedy_24_tokens: bfp16 and quant both identical to the GPU's

findings: auto (BFP16 copies until they stop fitting, then quantized) never used the quantized kernel on this model: BFP16 copies fill the limit first (49 layers at 20 GB, 62 at 25 GB), and from the layer that stops fitting even a quantized copy does not fit, so that layer and the rest go to the GPU. It ran exactly what bfp16 runs, and was removed; bfp16 is the default.
More layers on the NPU do not help while the devices take turns: 64 layers under BFP16 (294) against 49 (298).
quant pads rows: each of a piece's two streams rounds up to a multiple of 384, so 1,024 tokens run as 1,536 rows and 2,048 as 2,304.

The restructured multiply loop (kernels/bfp16_gemm/build/fast-loop-experiment.patch) is worth 16% on the quantized kernel and 3% on the BFP16 kernel, which stays at the DRAM limit. With bf16 sums as well the multiply alone falls to about 8 ms per 1,536 rows, but the GEMM stays at 13.3 ms: the unpacking core holds it (unpack_repeated).

ctest's mul-mat-npu-quant passed when the quantized kernel could not run (pointed at the BFP16 xclbin, the NPU failed and the GPU finished the test). Fixed with this record: the test fails on an NPU failure that was not injected.
